Contract.title: The contract is the approval surface; the separate brief is retired
Contract.Problem: The HTML brief was introduced to replace long GRACE 4 specifications, but a GRACE 5 contract is shorter than its brief and already states the behavioural delta, boundary, checks and decisions. The brief now duplicates that text with inflated prose, consumes preparation time and budget, and adds no decision the owner cannot take on the contract. Its independent writer did catch real contract defects, so the burden is the page and the fidelity machinery, not the independent read. The owner requested the brief's removal on 2026-11-17.
Contract.Change: The contract becomes the owner's approval surface. A new approval record binds the contract hash, each check definition and the decision; it carries no `brief-sha256`. Preparation keeps one lightweight independent contract read: an independent subagent receives the contract, the cited rules and read access, and returns findings only — a criterion its check cannot serve, an undefined term, a contradiction, a boundary that does not cover Change, or a cited path that does not exist. There is no page, no fidelity parser and no owner-facing brief; the author resolves the findings by editing the contract before the owner gate. `grace5 check` validates a brief only for a legacy approval that names one, and a new revision requires no brief. `run` and `close` impose no brief obligation on a new approval; `close.xml` omits `brief`. Historical briefs, approvals and close records remain readable and keep their hashes. `models/architecture/brief.md` and `templates/brief.html` leave the active surface; the parser remains only for legacy records. Prepare, orchestrate, execute and review guidance drop the brief writer and the brief handoff, and keep the findings-only independent contract read. Checks, receipts, complete-diff independent review, protected paths, approvals and closure stay as they are.

Constraints.Constraint: No command, check kind, receipt field, review rule or new approval artifact is added; the only lifecycle artifact removed is the brief.
An approval still binds the contract text, each check definition and the decision, is given by the owner alone, and is never inferred; removing the brief hash weakens no authority.
Historical records remain valid: a legacy approval that carries `brief-sha256` still requires that brief to match, while a new approval without it requires none.
L-04 is retired with the owner's stated burden and its removal criterion, and L-05 is amended to the contract-only binding; no other mechanism is added.
No version, pin, tag, migration boundary or migration row is registered by this change; migration implementation and tests may be prepared, and the release registers any boundary.
Checks, receipt provenance, independent complete-diff review, protected paths and closure are unchanged; no brief-derived assertion, summary or review substitute is accepted.

All seven prepared changes protect `models/architecture/templates/**`, and C-0012, C-0014, C-0017 and C-0018 also protect `models/architecture/brief.md`; this change executes only after all seven close or after their own approved material revisions remove the protection. Their briefs become history and are never rewritten, and C-0016's feasibility and discrimination guidance is relocated into the contract and prepare guidance before `brief.md` is deleted.

Every consumer is updated: `src/brief.ts` remains a legacy parser only; the `state.ts` and `close.ts` gates distinguish legacy from new; `approval.xsd` and `close.xsd` make the brief fields optional; `commands.md` drops the brief refusal phrases; `examples/defective-brief` stays a legacy fixture; conformance FS-12, FS-14, RV-04 and RV-10 are revised or retained as legacy cases; `m2-proposal.md` records the metric gap; L-04 is retired. The sysops graceopt brief metrics are a cross-repo consequence, not changed here.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No weakening of checks, independent review, receipt provenance, protected paths or closure.
No rewrite of historical briefs, approvals or close records.
No sysops METHOD.md or graceopt change; brief-derived metrics become unavailable for new changes and are a separate measurement decision.
No release, version, pin, tag or migration-table change.
No new approval artifact and no second decision.

Acceptance.Criterion: A new change with no brief can be approved, started, run, reviewed and closed, and neither `run` nor `close` names a missing brief.
A legacy change with a brief and `brief-sha256` still validates, runs and closes, and a mismatched legacy brief still refuses.
A contract edited after approval is still reported as altered after approval and treated as unapproved; the absence of a brief hides no alteration.
An approval without `brief-sha256` binds the contract hash and every check definition; a missing or wrong `Bound` still fails.
Review still receives the contract, complete diff, receipts and cited rules, writes findings and per-check adequacy, and requires no brief.
The retired brief documents leave the active surface, and active lifecycle guidance no longer instructs an independent brief or a brief handoff.
Historical examples and every closed change still read with no defect.
The kernel type-checks, and the generated packages and CLI reference remain current.
Preparation keeps one independent findings-only contract read before the owner gate; it creates no page and no fidelity parser, and the author resolves its findings in the contract.

Trace.Command: bun -e "const fs=require('fs'); const prepare=fs.readFileSync('skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md','utf8'); const files=['skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md','skills/grace5-orchestrate/SKILL.md','skills/grace5-execute/SKILL.md','skills/grace5-review/SKILL.md','models/architecture/method.md','models/architecture/authorization.md','models/architecture/commands.md']; const bad=files.filter(f=>/brief-<rev>|independent brief|brief writer|brief for approval/i.test(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8'))); if(!/independent contract read/i.test(prepare)){console.error('missing independent contract read'); process.exit(1);} if(bad.length){console.error('brief references: '+bad.join(', ')); process.exit(1);} console.log('briefless guidance: ok');"

Automated.Command: bun -e "const cp=require('child_process'); const ids=['C-0008-approval-executes','C-0009-decision-not-conversation','C-0011-clean-skill-source']; for (const id of ids){const r=cp.spawnSync('bun',['src/cli.ts','check',id]); if(r.status!==0){process.stdout.write(r.stdout);process.stderr.write(r.stderr);process.exit(1);}} console.log('legacy records: ok');"

Decisions.Decision: The owner reads the contract and answers in one statement; the contract's Problem, Change, Constraints, NonGoals, Acceptance, Affected, Checks and Decisions are the approval surface.
A new approval binds `contract-sha256`, each check's definition hash and the decision; `brief-sha256` is legacy and is neither required nor invented.
A legacy approval that carries `brief-sha256` keeps its brief obligation; a new approval without the attribute has none, and historical records are never rewritten.
`check`, `run` and `close` distinguish the two cases by the presence of `brief-sha256`; they do not infer a brief from a file on disk.
The brief documents and template leave the active surface; the parser remains only to validate legacy briefs and to keep historical examples and closed changes readable.
The independent review is unchanged and still reads the contract, complete diff, receipts and cited rules; it judges per-check adequacy and findings without a brief.
Brief-derived measurements become unavailable for new changes; the control center's method is not changed here and must decide their replacement separately.
This change registers no release or migration boundary; the implementation and tests may be prepared, and the release act registers the boundary it carries.

Pre-approval independence survives as a findings-only independent contract read: the reader is a subagent that did not write the contract, receives the contract, cited rules and read access, and returns findings; the author resolves them before the owner gate. No page, fidelity parser or owner-facing brief returns, and the final independent review is unchanged.

The seven prepared changes keep their existing briefs as history; all seven protect `templates/**`, and C-0012, C-0014, C-0017 and C-0018 protect `brief.md`, so this change is later in the execution order unless those changes' own approved revisions remove the protection.
